title: Westbrook School Committee — Finance Committee Meeting

fields.Location: Westbrook High School (Room 114), 125 Stroudwater St. (Hybrid via Zoom)

note: This summary highlights the meeting's key discussions and decisions, with direct quotes and timestamps for verification — it is not a substitute for watching the full meeting. This was the fifth and intended-final Finance Committee budget session (ran roughly 4.5 hours); no formal motions were made, but the chair settled items by informal show-of-hands tallies, including a 4–2 tally to remove the two secondary instructional coaches. The budget moves to the full School Committee as a recommendation. For complete context, nuance, and anything not covered, watch the full video at the link above. (Produced by: WestbrookCurrents.com)
attendance: Present: Finance Committee Chair Noreen Poitras, School Committee Chair Andrea Mancuso, School Committee Vice Chair Katy Rice, Allison Brunette, Erin Cavallaro, Dr. Flynn Ross. Absent: Brooke Reed.

blocks.x: Budget Schedule Change
Public Hearing & First Reading Pushed to April 8
Discussion Summary
Chair Mancuso said the budget's public hearing and first reading were expected tonight but will move to April 8 at 7:00 PM. (A first reading is the first of two required votes.)
The second reading, the final vote, will be April 13. The City Council budget presentation will be April 15 at 6:00 PM. The City rescheduled it to give the committee the extra week.
The Council's own first vote is April 27. The change gives the public fair notice once tonight's further budget changes are finalized.
Key Decisions
No vote — informational.
Action Items
None.
Working the Reduction List
Technology, Professional Development & Supplies
Discussion Summary

Technology ($111,000 proposed cut): This would delay the planned 11th-grade laptop-to-iPad transition, so older students keep their existing laptops, which are six-plus years old. It also trims middle and high school repair and maintenance lines. Dr. O'Donnell cautioned against reducing elementary device counts instead, citing disruption to curriculum and logistics.

Professional development ($86,250 proposed cut) and supplies ($12,132 proposed cut) drew strong pushback. Members cited real harm from last year's full elimination of professional development. Both were ultimately rejected and restored to the budget. The exception was a $3,000 One Westbrook professional development line, which was removed (see Final Decisions below).
Key Decisions
No formal vote — budget review (informal show-of-hands tallies; see Final Decisions below). No motion on any tally.
Action Items
None.
Athletics, Facilities & Staff Reductions (Tiers 1 & 2)
Discussion Summary

Athletics ($16,940) and Facilities ($42,350) reductions were largely confirmed as unspent amounts or items that can be put off. They were not real cuts to opportunities. A new idea for athletics-sponsorship revenue was floated for the committee to follow up on in the future.
Staff Tier 1 ($574,453.50 as proposed) eliminates several stipends, which are extra pay for added duties. It also eliminates:
The Equity Resource Coordinator.
The secondary literacy and math instructional coaches.
A vacant maintenance position.
A requested new network specialist position.
It reduces two staff schedules.

Before the staff tiers, City Administrator Angela Holmes gave a detailed cost breakdown for the School Resource Officer (SRO). The district pays 50% of SRO salary and benefits ($136,295.29), even though police data shows SROs spend 75–85% of their time on SRO-specific duties, not general patrol.

Staff Tier 2 eliminates a long-requested high school English teacher, a general education Ed Tech, the Multilingual Instructional Coach, and the two remaining elementary literacy/math coaches. Staff described this as getting close to “cutting into the bone.”
Key Decisions

No formal vote — an informal show-of-hands tally of 4–2 removed the two Tier 1 secondary instructional coaches. In favor of removing: Noreen Poitras, Allison Brunette, Katy Rice, Andrea Mancuso. Against: Dr. Flynn Ross, Erin Cavallaro. Brooke Reed was absent. No motion; informal show of hands.
Action Items
None.
Point / Counterpoint: Is the City Underfunding Its Schools?
A Pointed Exchange on City Cost-Sharing
Discussion Summary

As the reduction list review wound down, members voiced sharp frustration. They said peer communities devote a much higher share of their municipal budgets to schools than Westbrook does. They also said the district pays the City for SROs and athletic-field maintenance. Katy Rice acknowledged the City's recent help with street sweeping and playgrounds but said the City must contribute more.

Chair Mancuso suggested a way forward: send the budget on without further cuts and let the City Council and voters decide, rather than continue cutting tonight. No city commitment was reached on the record.
Key Decisions
No vote — discussion.
Action Items
None.
Point / Counterpoint

“I'm really struggling with the fact that we're sitting here talking about taking out staff that helps our teachers teach better...the districts around us, the cities around us, the percentage of the municipal budget that goes to the schools is at least 10% higher than what we're doing here...it's not okay anymore.”

“We can't keep saying that kids come first while funding them last...maybe [the City] can start with paying for SROs. And maybe they can start with not charging us $121,000 to mow and stripe our fields.”
“If the business I work for did that, you guys would not have groceries on your shelves.”
blocks.cite: Noreen Poitras, Finance Committee Chair (on asking the City for a tax-revenue estimate)

blocks.x: Final Decisions
What Stays, What's Cut, and What's Still Open
Discussion Summary
Chair Poitras summarized the committee's consensus:
Tier 1's stipends are kept. These are the high school's Building Assets, Reducing Risks stipends and coordinator, and the middle school's leadership stipends.
Tier 1's two secondary instructional coaches are removed on an informal 4–2 tally.
No Tier 2 cuts were made.
The general education Ed Tech is kept.
The English teacher is on the revisit list pending further class-size data.
The Multilingual Instructional Coach and elementary coaches stay in “for right now,” since their tally was paused and not finished.
Professional development and supplies stay funded, except the $3,000 One Westbrook professional development line, which was removed.
The technology, athletics, and facilities reductions proceed, along with the remaining Tier 1 staff items.
The budget's contingency line increases to 0.5% (about $77,000 more, per staff's estimate). A separate $25,000 emergency-repairs line is removed and folded into it.

A pending health-insurance rate update (maximum 11%, possibly lower) could allow further last-minute adjustment before April 15. No final total dollar figure or percentage increase was stated on the record. A “version three” budget was still being assembled as the meeting closed.
Key Decisions
No formal vote — the budget moves to the School Committee's April 8 public hearing and first reading as a recommendation, not an approved document.
Action Items
None.
